adds.title: LGBTQ rights in the Philippines - Wikipedia
adds.summary: National framework page (applies to Davao Region, which records no separate regional legislation; the national position plus any local ordinance of Davao City, the region's administrative center, is what a visitor stands under). Same-sex sexual activity is legal in the Philippines, but there is no national anti-discrimination statute - protection runs only in the basic-education context, with many local government non-discrimination ordinances filling the gap - and transgender people are not allowed to change their legal gender. Same-sex marriage and civil unions have no national recognition, the Family Code defining marriage as between a man and a woman, and the SOGIE Equality Bill has been repeatedly filed without enactment. The page's local-government-ordinances section lists Davao City (2012) among the localities with a non-discrimination ordinance, giving this region a dated, on-jurisdiction datapoint.

adds.title: Davao council bans discrimination vs gays, minority, differently abled - INQUIRER.net
adds.summary: INQUIRER.net (14 Dec 2012) reported that the Davao City council passed an ordinance banning discrimination against gays (LGBT people), minorities and differently-abled persons - a direct, dated report of the 2012 Davao City non-discrimination ordinance that the national LGBTQ-rights page cites as its Davao (2012) entry. Genuinely on-jurisdiction for Davao Region, whose administrative center is Davao City.

Same-sex sexual activity is legal in the Philippines, but there is no national anti-discrimination law - protection exists only in the basic-education context, with non-discrimination coverage left to local ordinances - and transgender people cannot change their legal gender.
